messages:
nina: Quick sync — need a final UX decision on how rule previews behave in the routing editor when multiple rules are expanded. QA found focus traps and visual jank on mobile widths.

omar: Reproduced. Two variants: A) allow multiple expanded cards (stacked) with internal scroll, B) only one expanded at a time (accordion). Each has tradeoffs for keyboard users.

leo: My leaning is B (single open). It simplifies focus management and reduces layout shift — easier to test in sim.

caro: Agree but we should keep a clear affordance to "Open all" in the header for power users. Also the preview header needs a compact status: "Matches 2/5" and a small chevron that is separately focusable.

nina: Good point. For keyboard: if we close the previous card when opening another, ensure focus stays on the triggering control not lost to body. Also add a brief live region note: "Rule X expanded" so SR users know which opened.

leo: Implementation note: use aria-expanded on the trigger; on open, set aria-live polite text to "Rule <name> expanded". Keep it brief.

omar: Copy tweak: expand trigger should read "Show details" / "Hide details" instead of icons-only. This helps discoverability for screen reader and keyboard users.

caro: Also we have a validation state for priority collisions. Current inline label "Priority invalid" was flagged as unclear. Proposed copy: "Priority conflict: two rules share the same priority. Reorder or change the number." Keep it under 80 chars.

nina: Sounds good. Also the rule reorder tooltip currently says "drag to reorder" — on touch devices drag is weird. Maybe change to "Drag or use the Move menu" and expose a three-dot menu with Move up/Move down actions.

leo: Regarding the drag handle: switch to an actual button element, aria-label "Move rule", and when activation opens a move menu expose keyboard commands (Alt+Up/Down) as hints.

omar: Performance note: animations were causing tab order issues; simplest fix is to postpone focus() until after transitionend or use CSS transform for animations (less layout thrash).

caro: For the preview simulation: add subtle match highlight when timeline hits a rule. Use 100ms fade-in and 250ms hold. Also add a small "matched" badge that appears. Reduce motion preference should disable animation.

sim-bot: Simulation run: label=\"single-expand-focus-check\" — 25 runs at widths [375, 768, 1200]. Failures: 4 runs at 375 where focus moved to body after expanding.

nina: Ok thats the repro. Omar, can you try the single-open approach and implement aria-live + postponing focus?

omar: Will do. I'll also add a unit test that simulates keyboard open/close and asserts document.activeElement remains the trigger after opening the next card.

leo: Copy for move menu actions: "Move up", "Move down", and for long lists show "Jump to top" / "Jump to bottom". Keep actions accessible via keyboard only when menu is open.

caro: UX microcopy for empty preview: instead of "No matches" use "No rules matched this request" and include a help link "Why rules didn’t match".

nina: Great. Quick QA checklist before merging: 1) single-open accordion behavior with aria-expanded, 2) focus persistence tests, 3) move menu keyboard actions + aria labels, 4) match highlight respects prefers-reduced-motion, 5) updated copy for priority conflict and empty preview.

omar: Targeting a small PR. Will ping when ready for re-run.

sim-bot: Rerun scheduled in 8m.

nina: Thanks team — small changes but big accessibility wins."
